mt: 'THE NEXT ELECTRONIC LITERATURE ORGANIZATION' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE MUSEUM, ITS LAB AND ITS CURATOR AT THEIR GRAIN; THE NAMES ITS WORKS STAND UNDER, A PEN NAME KEPT AS SUCH, NOT CARRIED
d: THE MUSEUM, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The NEXT is a digital art and writing museum, library, and preservation space created by the Electronic Literature Organization (ELO).' Key details: purpose ('Maintains and shares the cultural record of born-digital human expression'), contents ('over 3,000 born-digital literary works and dozens of collections ... dating from the mid-1980s onward'), support (the Electronic Literature Lab 'alongside the ELO'), leadership (Dene Grigar); two follow-up offers, the first to 'Search for a particular author or artist in the archive'. Six cards: the ELO, the-next.org (three), katyafarinsky.com, a YouTube talk by Dene Grigar.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the museum under its organization's name, the Overview says what it is, who made it, what it holds, who runs it and who leads it, from the museum's own pages and the ELO's.
findings: THE MUSEUM AT ITS GRAIN. 'Features over 3,000 born-digital literary works and dozens of collections (including hypertext, kinetic poetry, net art, interactive fiction, 3D, VR, and AI art)'. Wikipedia (saved): 'over 3,000 works by 2022'; the home page: 'the 48 collections of digital art and writing at The NEXT'. Card 3 carries the older figure, 'containing 30 collections', which Wikipedia gives as the museum's original holding ('originally housed 30 separate collections of 2,500 electronic literature works'). The ELO as maker agrees with the ELO Repository: 'Coming soon to ELO's newly created museum/library/preservation space, The NEXT'.

THE HOLDER AT ITS GRAIN. 'Hosted and supported by the Electronic Literature Lab at Washington State University Vancouver alongside the ELO' and 'Curated and directed through the Electronic Literature Lab by Dene Grigar.' The home page: 'The NEXT is supported by grants, donations, and commissions and managed by the Electronic Literature Lab', with 'Dene Grigar, Managing Director and Curator'. The grants, donations and commissions are not carried; the Wikipedia year of establishment ('Established 2011') is not given.

THE NAMES NOT CARRIED. The composition offers to 'Search for a particular author or artist in the archive' and names no author. The census row reads the museum's holding of authorship from Wikipedia's account of the Luesebrink Collection: 'Luesebrink created and published 27 of these works under the pen name M.D. Coverley', the works re-created by migration and kept under the name they were published under. Re-creation by migration, the museum's operation on a work, is likewise absent. 'AI art' stands among the contents; the home page lists 'Artificial Intelligence (AI)' among its collections' qualities; neither says how a machine's part in a work is attributed.

THE ADDRESS. Three cards give the museum at the-next.org ('Welcome Space | The NEXT', 'The NEXT About Space', 'The Electronic Literature Organization Archives - The NEXT'); the census row gives https://the-next.eliterature.org/.
analysis: An accurate composition of the museum, its maker and its holder. What the census reads it for, the names its works stand under and the migration that keeps a work under its author's name across obsolete software, is not carried.
per_note: Dene Grigar, the Electronic Literature Lab, WSU Vancouver and the ELO named; the museum's own pages carded.

atoms.reference: Works on obsolete software re-created by migration to newer systems, with as much metadata as possible where re-creation is not yet possible; works kept under the names they were published under (27 works under the pen name M.D. Coverley in the Luesebrink Collection).

evidence.record_quote: The NEXT has re-created these works by migrating them to newer systems.

Where recreating the work is not yet possible, such as Shockwave works like Jim Andrew's Nio , and Noah Wardrip Fruin et al.'s The Impermanence Agent , the NEXT has provided as much metadata as possible.

Luesebrink created and published 27 of these works under the pen name M.D. Coverley—and the NEXT Museum re-imagined, migrated, and developed video playthroughs of these works as they were written on now-obsolete software.

atoms.reference: Created as the ELO's museum/library/preservation space, out of the ELO Repository.

ELO has developed the ELO Repository that collects and/or manages online journals, works of electronic literature, community archives, and other digital materials for other organizations and makes them available to the public.
